title: Victoria Falls vs Iguazu Falls: Which Should You Visit?

faq.question: Which falls are bigger: Victoria Falls or Iguazu Falls?
faq.answer: Iguazu Falls is geographically larger, comprising a network of 275 individual falls stretching nearly 2.7 km (1.7 miles) across. Victoria Falls, while not as wide, is considered the single largest curtain of falling water in the world, with its main curtain over 1.7 km (1 mile) wide and dropping 108 meters (354 feet).

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Victoria Falls (Zambia/Zimbabwe)?
faq.answer: Yes, most nationalities require a visa for Zambia and/or Zimbabwe. The KAZA Uni-Visa (approx. $50 USD) is often recommended as it covers both countries and allows for day trips into Botswana. Always check current visa requirements based on your nationality before traveling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Iguazu Falls (Argentina/Brazil)?
faq.answer: Visa requirements depend on your nationality. Many countries, including the US and EU, do not require a visa for tourist visits to Argentina or Brazil. However, always verify the latest entry requirements for both countries well in advance, especially if you plan to visit both sides of the falls.

faq.question: Is it better to see Iguazu Falls from the Brazilian or Argentinian side?
faq.answer: Most travelers agree that the Argentinian side offers a more immersive experience with extensive walking trails that take you right over and into the falls, allowing for closer views. The Brazilian side provides more panoramic, wide-angle views of the entire system. Ideally, you should visit both sides to get the full perspective.

faq.question: What's the best currency to use at Victoria Falls?
faq.answer: In Zimbabwe, the USD is widely accepted and often preferred for tourist activities, hotels, and even some restaurants. In Zambia (Livingstone), the local currency is the Zambian Kwacha (ZMW), but USD is also commonly accepted for tourist services. It's always good to have small denominations of USD and some local currency.

faq.question: What's the best currency to use at Iguazu Falls?
faq.answer: On the Argentinian side, the Argentinian Peso (ARS) is the official currency, but USD is widely accepted and often preferred, especially for larger purchases. On the Brazilian side, the Brazilian Real (BRL) is the currency. It's best to have both local currencies or a travel card that offers good exchange rates.

faq.question: Is it safe to drink tap water in Victoria Falls or Iguazu Falls?
faq.answer: Generally, it is not recommended to drink tap water directly in either Victoria Falls or Iguazu Falls. While some hotels may filter their water, it's safest to stick to bottled water throughout your trip to avoid any stomach issues. This applies to both sides of the falls at both locations.

faq.question: Can I do a safari from Victoria Falls?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Victoria Falls is an excellent base for safari adventures. You can take a day trip to Chobe National Park in Botswana, famous for its large elephant populations and river safaris. Multi-day safaris into Hwange National Park in Zimbabwe or Kafue National Park in Zambia can also be arranged.
